messages:
cs-rep-john: Heads-up: ACME customers (multiple orgs) reporting sudden spike of 503s and long tail latencies to /v1/generate starting ~09:12 UTC. Sample request-id: req_8f3a2b. Error body: "upstream inference worker exited unexpectedly (signal 11)". Customer on 'hosted' with model redwood-llama-13b-q4.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0983. Pager duty: eng-sre oncall paged.

simon: I see a correlating worker churn in metrics — lots of container restarts on node gpu-7a2. Kernel log shows segfault from nvidia module in the inference process. Possible GPU OOM or illegal instruction.

maya: Customer repro steps (from their support ticket): single request, context ~4k tokens, batch 1 but they do many concurrent parallel requests (QPS ~120). They also enabled prefix prefetch on their route.

eng-sre-lee: quick triage: run `kubectl logs -n hosted runner-abcde -c infer --since=10m` and check /var/log/nvidia-*. Also pull `dmesg` for OOM/GPUPANIC. We need container stdout around crash time 09:12:07.

simon: pasted minimal log snippet: ```
2026-03-17T09:12:06Z infer[pid=4123]: kv_prefetch: prefetch batch=8 ctx_len=4096
2026-03-17T09:12:06Z infer[pid=4123]: allocating 11.2G for KV-cache
2026-03-17T09:12:07Z kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:af:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
2026-03-17T09:12:07Z infer[pid=4123]: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7fffe000
``` Suggests memory thrash then segfault.

support-ops: Customer billing team flagged these 503s as billing-impacting (they see retries and duplicated tokens). CS asking for ETA and whether we can disable retries or window them server-side.

maya: repro I ran locally in staging: curl replay with concurrent 100 clients + prefetch enabled reproduces segfault within ~30s. Command: `ab -n 10000 -c 100 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate` + route config `prefetch: true, max_prefetch_items: 32`.

eng-sre-lee: mitigation idea: 1) temporarily disable prefetch on affected hosted pool via config rollout (quick config change). 2) route heavy customers to smaller model variant (redwood-llama-7b) as fallback. 3) set worker eviction grace to higher so we avoid sudden cgroup kills while prefetched allocations in flight.

devrel-anna: can we add a hotpatch to API gateway that returns 429 for high concurrency from single customer token to avoid cascading faults? That would be faster than node-level patches.

simon: quick repro notes for root cause: it's interplay of prefetch + large ctx + bursty parallelism causing simultaneous large GPU allocations. One allocation path hits driver path that previously had a race — ends up as GPU reset and SIGSEGV. Suspect nvml driver/firmware on this GPU family.

oncall-bot: runbook step applied: applied temporary routing fallback for two orgs -> redirected to redwood-llama-7b at 09:27 UTC.

support-ops: Notified customers with temporary mitigation and asked them to reduce concurrency. Pending ETA to fix.

maya: repro steps I saved: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d @payload.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'` where payload.json contains 4096-token prompt. I also attached gdb backtrace from core (short): `#0 0x7f9d1a2c in kernel_driver_alloc+0x34
#1 0x7f9d1a77 in infer::kv_alloc...` (truncated).

simon: next engineering actions: (A) reproduce on dedicated repro node with same driver/firmware, (B) instrument allocations in runtime to fail gracefully (catch OOM and return 502 with friendly hint), (C) coordinate with infra to schedule a GPU firmware update if driver confirmed.

eng-sre-lee: I've opened GIT issue infra/runtime#612: "kv-prefetch triggers GPU reset under bursty concurrency" and assigned to simon + infra. Also capturing full coredump + nv-crashlog.

support-ops: CS wants a note on billing: can we suppress duplicate billing charge for retried tokens during the incident window 09:10-09:40 UTC? Finance here: escalate to billing ops.

oncall-bot: status update posted to #incidents at 09:40 UTC.

cs-rep-john: Customer asked for repro checklist and who owns the postmortem. Assigning to simon for root cause + maya for repro verification. I'll draft customer status email once we have RCA ETA. :+1:

simon: I'll try to get a reliable repro on a dedicated GPU replica today and update timeline in the issue. If we confirm driver/firmware we need downtime window for staged upgrades.

eng-sre-lee: Temp follow-ups: disable prefetch for hosted pool (DONE), create per-token concurrency cap in gateway (PR open), collect core+nvlog (done).

support-ops: closing interim customer notification loop. Will ping when billing decision made.

cs-rep-john: Thanks team — keeping this thread pinned for the incident until RMS/RCAs completed.
